result.scientific_strategy:
## c92ccfe2-1135-4ec4-bc5a-eded729fc461 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 196 successes out of 200 official episodes on the unchanged full-range reach-and-hold task. The strongest saved policy, checkpoint-100352 (working and best-known), succeeds on 1945/2000 = 97.25% of two disjoint 1000-episode full-range panels (97.2% seed 6000, 97.3% seed 8000), 99.5% on the reused seed-5000 selection panel and 98.0% on the reused task-reference panel. The deficit is not radial: every 6-20 cm radius band sits at 96.8-97.6%, while angle bins from -120 degrees to +180 degrees are 98-100% and the lower-left quadrant carries nearly all failures: [-150,-120) 72.9% (46/170) and [-180,-150) 96.6% (6/177). Failures are marginal in magnitude - 28 of 55 never enter the 1 cm tolerance (25 stopping 1.0-1.5 cm short) and 27 enter but hold fewer than 50 of the 100 required steps. The deficit therefore sits inside the trained 14-20 cm distribution, concentrated in a roughly 40-degree angular band. Code inspection of the shared observation mapping and protected arm model shows that an elbow-open inverse-kinematics branch is infeasible at some lower-left targets while the elbow-folded branch is feasible; the analogous positive-angle sector succeeds, so this is a candidate explanation rather than an established mechanism. A prior attempted targeted-coverage experiment was invalid before execution and adds no policy evidence.

**Lessons and limits:** The 14-20 cm training annulus was not the binding gap: near targets (6-14 cm) generalize at about 97.6%, no worse than the trained bands, and the deficit is in-distribution. Extended training of the same recipe gave no measured gain - checkpoint-100352 beats the later checkpoint-120832 on a shared 1000-episode panel (97.2% vs 96.2%) and on every paired comparison (12-1 over 1200 episodes), with checkpoint-115712 (96.7%, 7-1) and checkpoint-105472 (96.7%, 6-0) also behind. The training proxy plateaued at 0.93-0.97 after about 94,208 steps while measured failures stayed angularly structured. The baseline recipe already oversampled -165 to -115 degrees at 25%, so the residual does not establish that the band is merely absent from training; it leaves open whether stronger coverage is useful. Transfer from checkpoint-100352 preserves the learned observation/action semantics and broad reach-and-hold behavior, but its effect under a changed target distribution has not been measured. Limits: the two 1000-episode panels that drive the 97.25% estimate were also used to rank checkpoints, so they carry selection context; the 98.0% task-reference figure reuses one fixed 200-episode panel and is not independent confirmation. The angular decomposition is a descriptive summary of measured episodes. The link between the lower-left deficit and the shoulder-limit/IK-branch geometry is a code-inspection hypothesis about the task representation, not a measured property of the policy. The attempted experiment 2 record is invalid and unmeasured, so its 50% curriculum change cannot be treated as a negative or positive result.

**Open questions:** Is the lower-left deficit a training-coverage or optimization artifact that additional targeted sampling can remove, or a stable property of the arm's joint-limit and IK-reference geometry? Would a distribution, reward or observation change remove that band without disturbing the near-perfect sectors? Can the unresolved hold-boundary oscillation at lateral/positive angles reappear under a changed target distribution? These uncertainties remain open; their presence does not prescribe an experiment or imply that any one intervention is required.
